items.text: Understand that CloudWatch is AWS's central monitoring and observability service
Explain the difference between CloudWatch Metrics and CloudWatch Logs
Know the 80% CPU utilization rule and why it matters
Understand what Unix epoch timestamps are and why AI cannot reliably convert them
Explain the difference between CloudWatch and CloudTrail and when to use each
Understand what inference profiles are and the difference between global and regional profiles
Navigate to CloudWatch Log Groups and Log Streams in the AWS Console
Use CloudWatch Log Insights to run basic queries on log data
Use the AI natural language query generator to create Log Insights queries without knowing the syntax
Use the AI Summarize Results feature to analyze hundreds of log entries quickly
Convert a Unix millisecond timestamp to a human-readable date using Python or an online tool
Create a CloudWatch alarm for CPU utilization on an EC2 instance
Answer questions distinguishing CloudWatch (performance) from CloudTrail (API audit)
Identify what HTTP 200, 4xx, and 500 status codes indicate
Know that the AI Summarize feature in CloudWatch Log Insights launched globally in August 2024
